common.codePlaceholder: From your authenticator app, or a backup code

changeEmail.heading: Email
changeEmail.intro: The address you sign in with. Changing it needs your current password.
changeEmail.introMfa: The address you sign in with. Changing it needs your current password and a two-factor code.
changeEmail.changedBody: Your sign-in email has been updated.

changePassword.heading: Password
changePassword.intro: Change the password you use to sign in. Your other devices will be signed out.

devices.heading: Linked devices
devices.description: Televisions, wall displays and other screens you've signed in by scanning a code. They stay signed in until you remove them, and they can't reach the control panel.
devices.emptyBody: No linked devices yet. On the TV or display, open iSputnik and choose <bold>Link a TV or display</bold> — then scan the code it shows with this phone.
devices.nameHint: Leave it empty to go back to what the browser reports.
devices.confirmRevokeBody: That device is signed out immediately and will need authorizing again to come back. Nothing else about your account changes, and nothing is deleted.

mfa.heading: Two-factor authentication
mfa.intro: Ask for a one-time code at sign-in — from an authenticator app or sent to your email — so a stolen password alone can't reach your account.
mfa.onBodyEmail: You'll enter a code sent to {{email}} when you sign in.
mfa.onBodyTotp: You'll enter a code from your authenticator app when you sign in.
mfa.noBackupCodes: No backup codes left — regenerate a set.
mfa.noEmailBody: Your codes have nowhere to go until an administrator sets email up again. Use a backup code to sign in meanwhile.
mfa.methodTotpDesc: A rolling code from Google Authenticator, Authy, Apple Passwords… Works offline and never leaves your phone.
mfa.methodEmailDesc: A one-time code sent to {{email}} each time you sign in. Nothing to install.
mfa.methodEmailNoteAvailable: Less secure: codes travel by email, so anyone who can read that inbox can get in.
mfa.methodEmailNoteUnavailable: Unavailable — this server can't send email. An administrator sets it up in Control panel → Settings → Email.
mfa.scanIntro: Scan this with your authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Authy, Apple Passwords…), then enter the 6-digit code it shows to confirm.
mfa.manualEntryIntro: Can't scan? Enter this key manually:
mfa.emailStepIntro: We sent a 6-digit code to <bold>{{email}}</bold>. Enter it to confirm the address can reach you. It expires in {{minutes}} minutes.
mfa.saveNowBodySetup: Each code lets you sign in once if your second factor is out of reach — a lost authenticator, or an inbox you can't get to. They won't be shown again.
mfa.regenerateIntro: Confirm your password and a current two-factor code. This replaces your existing backup codes with a fresh set.
mfa.newCodesBody: These replace your old codes, which no longer work. They won't be shown again.
mfa.disableIntro: Your account will be protected by your password alone. Confirm your password and a current two-factor code to turn it off.

passkeys.heading: Passkeys
passkeys.intro: Sign in with your fingerprint, face or device PIN instead of typing a password. The key itself never leaves your device, so there's nothing to steal or phish — and because your device checks it's you, no one-time code is needed either.
passkeys.notAvailableTitle: Passkeys aren't available on this server
passkeys.notAvailableBody: They need the server to be reached over HTTPS at a domain name — an address like https://library.example.com. On a home network reached by IP address, browsers won't allow them at all. Your administrator can set this up.
passkeys.unsupportedBody: Try a current version of Safari, Chrome, Edge or Firefox.
passkeys.emptyList: No passkeys yet. Add one for the device you use most.
passkeys.addModalIntro: Confirm your password, then your device will ask for your fingerprint, face or PIN.
passkeys.cancelledRetry: That was cancelled before your device finished. Try again.
passkeys.confirmRemoveBody: That device won't be able to sign in with a passkey any more. Your password and two-factor sign-in still work, and your other passkeys are not affected.

sharedLinks.heading: Shared links
sharedLinks.intro: Every guest link you have created that has not been revoked. Anyone holding one of these can open what it points at without signing in, until it expires. The link addresses themselves are not stored and cannot be shown again — if you have lost one, revoke it and create a new one.
sharedLinks.emptyBody: You have not created any guest links. You can make one from the Share button on any book, photo, or album.
sharedLinks.expiredNote: These no longer grant access. Revoking them just clears them from this list.
sharedLinks.confirmRevokeBodyExpired: This link has already expired, so nobody can use it. Revoking removes it from the list.
sharedLinks.confirmRevokeBodyActive: Anyone still holding this link will lose access immediately. Nothing is deleted, and people you shared with by account keep their access.
